method_card.title: Past Holidays and Experiences
method_card.content:
This lesson is the central grammar challenge of Theme 6: the contrast between the preterite and the imperfect tense. Spanish requires both in a past holiday narrative — unlike French, which collapses both into a single perfect tense.

SpanishEnglish
fui (preterite of ir)I went
visité (preterite of visitar)I visited
comí (preterite of comer)I ate
nadé (preterite of nadar)I swam
hice (preterite of hacer)I did / I made
era (imperfect of ser)it was (description)
hacía sol / calor / fríoit was sunny / hot / cold
había (imperfect of haber)there was / there were
se veían (imperfect of verse)you could see (description)
me lo pasé genialI had a brilliant time
fue increíbleit was incredible
sin embargohowever
ademásalso / moreover

Grammar focus — preterite vs imperfect: Use the preterite for completed, single events: fui a Roma (I went to Rome), comí pizza (I ate pizza). Use the imperfect for descriptions, ongoing background, or repeated past actions: el hotel era bonito (the hotel was nice), hacía calor todos los días (it was hot every day). Both tenses often appear together: Estaba en la playa cuando empezó a llover (I was on the beach when it started to rain) — the ongoing background uses the imperfect; the sudden interruption uses the preterite.

Model paragraph: El verano pasado fui de vacaciones a Portugal con mi familia. El hotel era muy cómodo y hacía sol todos los días. Visité varios monumentos y comí mucho marisco. Sin embargo, un día perdí mi móvil — ¡fue un desastre! (Last summer I went on holiday to Portugal with my family. The hotel was very comfortable and it was sunny every day. I visited several monuments and ate a lot of seafood. However, one day I lost my mobile — it was a disaster!)
steps: Learn the key preterite forms for holiday verbs: fui, visité, comí, hice, nadé
Master the imperfect for descriptions: era, hacía, había, estaba
Practise the contrast — preterite for events, imperfect for background
Build extended narratives combining both tenses with connectives

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — past holiday narratives appear in every writing and speaking series

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Hacía mucho calor y fui a la playa todos los días.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Hacía mucho calor — note hacía is imperfect (description of ongoing weather). It was very hot.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Fui a la playa = I went to the beach (preterite — completed action). Todos los días = every day.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: It was very hot and I went to the beach every day.

worked_examples.question: Which tense? 'El hotel _____ (ser) muy bonito y _____ (tener) una piscina.' — era/fue and tenía/tuvo?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Both verbs describe what the hotel was like — an ongoing description, not a single completed event.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Descriptions in the past use the imperfect: era (it was, imperfect of ser) and tenía (it had, imperfect of tener). Fue and tuvo would imply a completed, one-off event.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: El hotel era muy bonito y tenía una piscina. Imperfect for descriptions.

bronze.question: Match the Spanish preterite forms to their English meaning
Match the Spanish imperfect forms to their English meaning
Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: en el mar con mis amigos.

gaps.correct_explain: hacía (imperfect) is used for weather descriptions in the past. Hizo (preterite) is also accepted for stating the weather that day.

wrong.hace: hace is the present tense. Ayer (yesterday) requires a past tense.
wrong.hará: hará is the future tense. Ayer is past.

gaps.correct_explain: nadé is the yo preterite of nadar — a completed action yesterday.

wrong.nado: nado is the present tense. Ayer requires the preterite.
wrong.nadaba: nadaba is the imperfect — used for habitual or ongoing past actions, not a single event yesterday.

gaps.correct_explain: era is the imperfect of ser. Use it for describing what the hotel was like — an ongoing characteristic.

wrong.fue: fue is the preterite of ser. For a description of what it was like (not a single event), use the imperfect era.
wrong.es: es is the present tense. You are describing a past hotel.

gaps.correct_explain: tenía is the imperfect of tener. Use it to describe what something had as an ongoing feature.

wrong.tuvo: tuvo is the preterite of tener. For describing features of a place, use the imperfect.

bronze.question: What does 'Hacía buen tiempo y fui de compras' mean?
options: The weather was good and I went shopping
The weather is good and I go shopping
The weather will be good and I will go shopping
The weather was bad and I went shopping

bronze.question: Which sentence correctly describes a past holiday in Spanish?
options: El hotel era cómodo y fui a la playa todos los días.
El hotel fue cómodo y iba a la playa todos los días.
El hotel estaba cómodo y fue a la playa todos los días.
El hotel era cómodo y voy a la playa todos los días.

bronze.source_text: Hacía calor y nadamos en el mar. El agua estaba muy fría.
model_answers: It was hot and we swam in the sea. The water was very cold.
hints: el agua estaba = the water was

silver.question: Complete the sentence
silver.english: I **stayed** in a luxury hotel and the room **had** sea views.
sentence_parts: en un hotel de lujo y la habitación

gaps.correct_explain: alojé is the yo preterite of alojarse (to stay). The action of staying is completed.

wrong.alojaba: alojaba is the imperfect. Use the preterite for the single completed act of staying.

gaps.correct_explain: tenía is the imperfect — describing what the room had as an ongoing feature.

wrong.tuvo: tuvo is the preterite of tener. For ongoing descriptions, use the imperfect.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: El año pasado fui a Portugal y el tiempo fue muy bueno cada día.
silver.explanation: Cada día (every day) signals a repeated, ongoing background condition — use the imperfect: era (it was) or hacía buen tiempo (the weather was good). Fue (preterite) implies a single, one-off event.
silver.translation: Last year I went to Portugal and the weather was very good every day.

silver.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
silver.english: I was on the beach when it started to rain.

distractor_labels.estuve: wrong tense — estuve is preterite (I was, completed event). For ongoing background use imperfect: estaba

silver.source_text: I stayed in a youth hostel. It was cheap but comfortable.
model_answers: Me alojé en un albergue juvenil. Era barato pero cómodo.

silver.correct_text: Estábamos comiendo cuando empezó a llover y fuimos al hotel.

gold.source_text: Last summer the weather was great and I swam in the sea every day. I visited several monuments and the food was delicious. In the future I would like to go back because I had a brilliant time.
model_answers: El verano pasado hacía muy buen tiempo y nadé en el mar todos los días. Visité varios monumentos y la comida estaba deliciosa. En el futuro me gustaría volver porque me lo pasé genial.

Check: imperfect for weather (hacía), preterite for completed actions (nadé, visité), imperfect for description (estaba), conditional (me gustaría). Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences about grammar accuracy","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

gold.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
gold.english: Every morning we were swimming in the sea and in the afternoon we sunbathed.

distractor_labels.nadamos: wrong tense — nadamos is preterite/present; habitual past actions use the imperfect: nadábamos
distractor_labels.tomamos: wrong tense — tomamos is preterite/present; habitual actions need the imperfect: tomábamos
distractor_labels.las: wrong article — tarde is singular feminine, so use la not las

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a tourist information office in Spain. You tell the assistant about your last holiday and ask for recommendations.

bullets.prompt: Greet the assistant and say where you went on holiday last year.
bullets.model_answer: ¡Buenos días! El año pasado fui de vacaciones a Portugal.

bullets.prompt: Describe what the weather was like and what you did.
bullets.model_answer: Hacía mucho sol y visité varios monumentos. También nadé en el mar.
bullets.note: imperfect (hacía) for weather + preterite (visité, nadé) for completed actions

bullets.prompt: Give your opinion of the holiday.
bullets.model_answer: Me lo pasé genial porque el hotel era muy cómodo y la gente era muy amable.

bullets.prompt: Ask the assistant to recommend somewhere to visit this summer.
bullets.model_answer: ¿Puede recomendarme un sitio para visitar este verano?

gold.question: Listen and type what you hear
gold.audio_text: El verano pasado fui a Portugal con mi familia. Hacía mucho sol y me lo pasé genial.
gold.correct_text: El verano pasado fui a Portugal con mi familia. Hacía mucho sol y me lo pasé genial.
gold.translation: Last summer I went to Portugal with my family. It was very sunny and I had a brilliant time.

gold.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
gold.sentence: Si hiciera buen tiempo, iría a la playa y estaba nadando en el mar.
gold.explanation: In a hypothetical si clause with the imperfect subjunctive (hiciera), the main clause needs the conditional: estaría nadando (I would be swimming), not estaba nadando (I was swimming — imperfect).
gold.translation: If the weather were good, I would go to the beach and would be swimming in the sea.
